{{short description|American basketball player (born 2003)}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Julian Reese | image = Julian Reese (54424016534) (cropped).jpg | caption = Reese in 2025 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2003|6|30}} | birth_place = [[Baltimore, Maryland]], U.S. | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 9 | weight_lb = 230 | league = | team = Free agent | position = [[Power forward]] | number = | high_school = [[Saint Frances Academy (Baltimore)|St. Frances Academy]]
(Baltimore, Maryland) | college = [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] (2021–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team1 = [[Raptors 905]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|end}} | team2 = [[Washington Wizards]] | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team3 = →[[Capital City Go-Go]] | highlights = }} '''Julian Reese''' (born June 30, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played college basketball for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]]. ==Early life and high school== Coming out of high school, Reese was rated as a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]].{{cite web |last1=Giambalvo |first1=Emily |title=Julian Reese, a four-star forward from Baltimore, commits to Maryland for 2021 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/05/10/julian-reese-four-star-forward-baltimore-commits-maryland-2021/ |website=The Washington Post |access-date=March 8, 2025}} ==College career== As a [[freshman]] in 2021-22, Reese averaged 5.7 points and 4.4 rebounds in 17.7 minutes per game.{{cite web |last1=Markus |first1=Don |title=Why Baltimore native Julian Reese might be the most important player for the surprising Terps |url=https://www.thebaltimorebanner.com/sports/college-sports/why-baltimore-native-julian-reese-might-be-the-most-important-player-for-the-surprising-terps-DI4OSRCKRJCZJPDAQV7YQNEMZA/ |website=The Baltimore Banner |access-date=March 8, 2025}} Ahead of the 2022-23 season, he became a full-time starter for the Terrapins.{{cite web |last1=Lee |first1=Edward |title=Maryland’s Julian Reese put in the work to become more valuable |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2025/02/01/julian-reese-maryland-mens-basketball-free-throws/ |website=Baltimore Sun |access-date=March 8, 2025}} On February 16, 2023, Reese helped the Terrapins to an upset win over #3 [[2022–23 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]].{{cite web |last1=Lee |first1=Edward |title=Julian Reese leaves mark as his Maryland men’s basketball career nears an end |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2025/03/04/julian-reese-leaves-mark-maryland-mens-basketball/ |website=Baltimore Sun |access-date=8 March 2025}} He finished the 2022-23 season averaging 11.4 points, 7.2 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game, earning [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] honorable mention.{{cite web |last1=Vessels |first1=Chandler |title=Julian Reese announces return to Maryland for senior season |url=https://www.on3.com/college/maryland-terrapins/news/julian-reese-announces-return-to-maryland-for-senior-season-angel-reese/ |website=On3.com |access-date=March 8, 2025}} In 2023-24, Reese averaged 13.7 points, 9.5 rebounds and 1.9 blocks per game and earned all-Big Ten honorable mention.{{cite web |last1=Champion |first1=Brandon |title=Maryland basketball star to return for senior season |url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/2024/03/maryland-basketball-star-to-return-for-senior-season.html |website=MLive.com |access-date=March 8, 2025}} On November 11, 2024, he put up 21 points and nine rebounds in a victory over [[2024–25 Florida A&M Rattlers basketball team|Florida A&M]].{{cite web |last1=Hirt |first1=Gibson |title=Julian Reese is back on track after slow start for Maryland |url=https://wmucsports.net/julian-reese-is-back-on-track-after-slow-start-for-maryland/ |website=WMUC.com |access-date=8 March 2025}} On January 23, 2025, Reese put up 27 points, 17 rebounds, and three blocks in a blowout win over [[2024–25 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]].{{cite web |last1=Lu |first1=Alan |title=Observing Derik Queen, Kasparas Jakucionis, and Julian Reese in the Maryland-Illinois Game |url=https://www.nbascoutinglive.com/observing-derik-queen-kasparas-jakucionis-and-julian-reese-in-the-maryland-illinois-game/ |website=NBA Scouting Live |access-date=8 March 2025}} On January 29, he put up 14 points and eight rebounds in a victory over [[2024–25 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]].{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Maryland's Julian Reese, Angel Reese's brother, has emerged as vital piece for pleasantly surprising Terrapins |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/marylands-julian-reese-angel-reeses-brother-has-emerged-as-vital-piece-for-pleasantly-surprising-terrapins/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=8 March 2025}} On March 5, Reese tallied six points and four rebounds in a win over [[2024–25 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]].{{cite web |last1=Goon |first1=Kyle |title=Kyle Goon: Julian Reese represented the Terps’ potential. As a senior, he has delivered. |url=https://www.thebaltimorebanner.com/sports/college-sports/julian-reese-terps-basketball-willard-march-madness-FZLR7WREORDQ5GMFTLSFJ6ZLVY/ |website=The Baltimore Banner |access-date=8 March 2025}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Reese joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web|title=Angel Reese's Brother, Julian, Signs with the Lakers for NBA Summer League|url=https://www.si.com/high-school/maryland/angel-reese-s-brother-julian-signs-with-the-lakers-for-nba-summer-league-01jz1jkf9vkt|access-date=July 5, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}} On October 17, 2025, Reese signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web |last1=Blake |first1=Silverman |title='Congrats to My Baby Brother': Angel Reese's Brother Julian Signs With Raptors |url=https://www.si.com/nba/angel-reese-brother-julian-signs-with-raptors |publisher=si.com |access-date=18 October 2025}} On February 28, 2026, Reese was signed to a [[Two-way_contract#Basketball|two-way contract]] by the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web |last1=Golding |first1=Jaden |title=Julian Reese Signs A Two-Way Deal With The Washington Wizards |url=https://www.si.com/college/maryland/basketball/julian-reese-signs-a-two-way-deal-with-the-washington-wizards-01kjk9j1kvw9 |website=Sports Illustrated |access-date=3 March 2026 |date=1 March 2026}} His first game with the team came two days later, against the [[2025–26 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]], where he was pressed into service as the Wizards' starting center{{cite web |last1=Conlin |first1=Bennett |title=Former Terps standout Julian Reese makes NBA debut with Wizards |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2026/03/02/julian-reese-makes-nba-debut-wizards/ |website=Baltimore Sun |access-date=3 March 2026 |date=2 March 2026}} as all the team's other big men were out with injury.{{cite web |title=Wizards' Julian Reese: Logs 28 minutes in debut |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-julian-reese-logs-28-minutes-in-debut/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=3 March 2026 |language=en |date=2 March 2026}} Reese went 1-for-3 in shooting on the night, earning his first two points as an NBA player, in addition to four rebounds and three steals. Reese also committed three turnovers and fouled out after almost 28 minutes that same night.{{cite web |title=Houston Rockets vs Washington Wizards Mar 2, 2026 Box Scores |url=https://www.nba.com/game/hou-vs-was-0022500879/box-score |website=NBA |access-date=3 March 2026 |language=en |date=2 March 2026}} On March 5, Reese put up a double-double with 18 points and 20 rebounds, 10 offensive and 10 defensive, in a 122–112 loss to the [[2025–26 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]]. He became the first player since [[Antawn Jamison]] in 2010 to put up 10 offensive and 10 defensive rebounds in a game in Wizards franchise history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/other-sports/wizards-news-angel-reeses-brother-trae-youngs-debut-monster|title=Angel Reese’s brother takes over Trae Young’s Wizards debut with monster game|website=ClutchPoints|last=Villas|first=Rexwell|date=March 5, 2026|access-date=March 5, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-julian-reese-records-monster-double-double/|title=Wizards' Julian Reese: Records monster double-double|website=CBS Sports|date=March 5, 2026|access-date=March 5, 2026}} On March 25, Reese had another double-double with 26 points, 17 rebounds, a steal, and a block across 30 minutes of a 133-110 win over the Jazz.{{Cite web |last=español |first=Leer en |date=2026-03-26 |title=Led by Reese and Riley, Wizards snap 16-game losing streak, beat Jazz 133-110 |url=https://apnews.com/article/jazz-wizards-score-dea3da8ff11dbbb92f07b4942a3668cc |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=AP News |language=en}} On August 20, 2026, Reese was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]]. After the trade, he was released by the Nuggets.{{Cite web |date=2026-08-20 |title=NUGGETS ACQUIRE FUTURE UNPROTECTED FIRST AND SECOND ROUND PICKS IN SIGN AND TRADE |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-future-unprotected-first-and-second-round-picks-sign-and-trade |access-date=2026-08-21 }} == Personal life == Reese is the brother of [[WNBA]] All-Star [[Angel Reese]].{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Glenn |title=Appreciate The Four-Year Journey Of Maryland Men’s Basketball’s Julian Reese |url=https://pressboxonline.com/2025/02/18/glenn-clark-appreciate-the-four-year-journey-of-maryland-mens-basketballs-julian-reese/ |website=Pressbox Online |access-date=8 March 2025}}{{cite web |last1=Aizin |first1=Rebecca |title=All About Angel Reese's Brother Julian Reese |url=https://people.com/all-about-angel-reese-brother-julian-reese-8611682 |website=People.com |access-date=8 March 2025}} Reese's mother played college basketball for [[UMBC Retrievers women's basketball|UMBC]], where she was inducted into the Athletics Hall of Fame and her number 10 jersey was retired.{{cite web |last1=Gilpin |first1=Matt |title=The Reeses: A Terp Family Affair |url=https://umterps.com/news/2022/1/25/terrapin-club-the-reeses-a-terp-family-affair |publisher=[[University of Maryland Athletics]] |title=Reeses may UMd hoops a family affair |url=https://www.wypr.org/show/sports-at-large-with-milton-kent/2021-11-15/reeses-may-umd-hoops-a-family-affair |publisher=[[WYPR]] |access-date=July 23, 2023 |date=November 15, 2021 |archive-date=July 23, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723184650/https://www.wypr.org/show/sports-at-large-with-milton-kent/2021-11-15/reeses-may-umd-hoops-a-family-affair |url-status=live }} She later played
